flawed_step: 0028: Bipartiteness of H does not imply that the two endpoints of an added ear have different colors (one red and one blue). They may have the same color.
counterexample: Let H be the 4-cycle v1-v2-v3-v4-v1, colored v1,v3 red and v2,v4 blue. Add the ear P=v1-x-v3, whose endpoints v1 and v3 are both red. Embed H as a square and P inside it. The resulting graph G has three faces, with boundary cycles v1-v2-v3-x-v1, v1-x-v3-v4-v1, and v1-v2-v3-v4-v1, all of length 4. It is 2-connected: deleting any one of its five vertices leaves a connected graph. Thus G satisfies the hypotheses and this is a legitimate ear addition, but its endpoints are not colored red and blue as asserted in step 0028.
assessment_summary: Steps through 0027 are supportable, but step 0028 makes a false inference about the colors of an ear's endpoints. The explicit 2-connected plane graph above satisfies the even-face hypothesis and directly contradicts that inference, so the proof as written is invalid.
